copy.title: 4.2 The Water Cycle
paragraph: Every day, the sun heats the surface of the ocean, and a thin layer of
liquid water turns into invisible water vapour. The vapour rises into
the sky, where it cools and gathers into clouds. The salt, however,
never makes it onto the journey: it stays behind in the sea, so the sky only
copy.script: In step one, the sun heats the ocean, and liquid water becomes invisible water vapor, rising into the sky. While a single drop can stay airborne for 10 days, the salt stays behind in the sea. The sky only takes the pure water.
copy.tagline: Turn any document into a hand-illustrated explainer video.
